lean.statement:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] {mu pi nu : Measure State} {gamma : Measure (State × State)}
  (hgamma : DisplacementInterpolation.IsQuadraticOptimalCoupling gamma mu nu) (hscore : SmoothFiniteScoreDomain mu pi)
  (hmu : Integrable (fun x => ‖x‖ ^ 2) mu) (hnu : Integrable (fun x => ‖x‖ ^ 2) nu),
  |∫ (z : State × State), ⟪gradient (RNLogRatio.logRatio mu pi) z.1, z.2 - z.1⟫ ∂gamma| ≤
    √(information mu pi hscore) * (WassersteinSpace.wassersteinDistance mu nu).toReal

decoder_context: State abbreviates EuclideanSpace ℝ ι for the finite index type ι, with its standard Borel measurable structure. mu, pi and nu are measures on this space, and gamma is a measure on its Cartesian square.

RNLogRatio.logRatio mu pi is MeasureTheory.llr mu pi: x ↦ Real.log ((mu.rnDeriv pi x).toReal). The RN representative is the library-selected one. Real.log and ENNReal.toReal are total functions, including Real.log 0 = 0 and ENNReal.toReal infinity = 0.
gradient phi x is the Riesz inverse of the real Frechet derivative fderiv at x. This is a total definition, with zero at points where phi is not differentiable.
SmoothFiniteScoreDomain mu pi consists of mu ≪ pi, mu-almost-everywhere DifferentiableAt ℝ (RNLogRatio.logRatio mu pi), and integrability under mu of x ↦ ‖gradient (RNLogRatio.logRatio mu pi) x‖^2.
information mu pi hscore is the real Bochner integral under mu of the squared norm of this gradient. The argument hscore is a proof of the domain condition just described.
Transport.IsCoupling gamma mu nu means that the two coordinate pushforwards of gamma equal mu and nu. It does not itself impose probability normalization or finite total mass.

DisplacementInterpolation.IsQuadraticOptimalCoupling gamma mu nu means that gamma is a coupling and that its extended-nonnegative integral of quadraticCost equals the infimum of those costs over all couplings of mu and nu.

quadraticCost(x,y) is ENNReal.ofReal(‖x-y‖^2). WassersteinSpace.wassersteinDistance mu nu is the extended-nonnegative square root (power 1/2) of that infimum. The suffix toReal converts this extended-nonnegative value to a real number.

reconstruction.text: For every finite index type iota, let E = EuclideanSpace(R, iota) with its standard Borel structure. For all measures mu, pi, nu on E and gamma on E x E, put ell(x) = Real.log((mu.rnDeriv pi x).toReal), using the library-selected Radon-Nikodym representative, and s(x) = gradient ell x, the Riesz inverse of the real Frechet derivative. For a measure eta on E x E, let C(eta) be the extended-nonnegative integral of ENNReal.ofReal(||x-y||^2), and let K(mu,nu) be the infimum of C(eta) over all measures eta whose coordinate pushforwards are mu and nu. Suppose gamma has these coordinate pushforwards and C(gamma) = K(mu,nu); mu is absolutely continuous with respect to pi; ell is differentiable at mu-almost every point; x -> ||s(x)||^2 is integrable under mu; and x -> ||x||^2 is integrable under both mu and nu. Then |integral_(E x E) <s(x), y-x> dgamma(x,y)| <= sqrt(integral_E ||s(x)||^2 dmu(x)) * (K(mu,nu)^(1/2)).toReal. The integrals outside the definition of C are real Bochner integrals, the displayed sqrt is the real square root, and K^(1/2) is the extended-nonnegative square root. Real.log, ENNReal.toReal, and the gradient are total definitions: Real.log(0) = 0, ENNReal.toReal(+infinity) = 0, and the gradient is zero where ell is not differentiable. No probability normalization or finite-total-mass assumption is imposed.

source.anchor: Section 1.3, printed/PDF page 5, general Glauber update steps 2–3; https://arxiv.org/pdf/2307.13826v4#page=5. Two short formula/instruction excerpts below. ASTIS context paraphrase (not source quotation): the source uses a distribution on Omega subset of {0,1}^V, a finite site set V and a starting configuration X_t in Omega; step 2 applies to every w != v. The preceding uniform-site selection step is outside this fixed-site comparison.
source.original_text:
X_{t+1}(w) = X_t(v).
Choose X_{t+1}(v) from the conditional Gibbs distribution μ(σ(v) = · | σ(w) = X_t(w) for all w ≠ v).

lean.statement: ∀ {n : ℕ} (X : Fin (n + 1) → Type u_1) [inst : (j : Fin (n + 1)) → MeasurableSpace (X j)] (μ : Measure ((j : Fin (n + 1)) → X j)) [inst_1 : IsFiniteMeasure μ] (i : Fin (n + 1)) [inst_2 : StandardBorelSpace (X i)] [inst_3 : Nonempty (X i)] [MeasurableSingletonClass ((j : Fin n) → X (i.succAbove j))] (x : (j : Fin (n + 1)) → X j), μ {y | (fun j => y (i.succAbove j)) = fun j => x (i.succAbove j)} ≠ 0 → (CoordinateHeatBath.heatBath X μ i) x = μ[|{y | (fun j => y (i.succAbove j)) = fun j => x (i.succAbove j)}]
decoder_context: Fin (n+1) is the finite index type; i.succAbove : Fin n → Fin (n+1) enumerates the indices other than i in increasing order. The universe u_1 is arbitrary.
e_i is the measurable equivalence x ↦ ((fun j => x (i.succAbove j)), x i), with inverse reinserting the selected coordinate.

For ν = μ.map e_i, let κ = condDistrib Prod.snd Prod.fst ν. condDistrib Y Z ν is the selected regular conditional-distribution Markov kernel, defined as the conditional kernel of ν.map (fun a => (Z a, Y a)); it is characterized ν.map Z-almost everywhere.
CoordinateHeatBath.heatBath X μ i x = (e_i.symm)_# (dirac ((e_i x).1) × κ ((e_i x).1)); measure map denotes pushforward, and the product is the product of measures.

μ[|s] denotes ProbabilityTheory.cond μ s, defined as (μ s)⁻¹ • μ.restrict s. The scalar is ENNReal with totalized inverse. IsFiniteMeasure means finite total mass; no normalization to mass one is built into that class.

reconstruction.text: Let n be any natural number, let (X_j) indexed by Fin(n+1) be measurable spaces, and let μ be a finite measure on their dependent product Ω = ∏_j X_j. Fix i ∈ Fin(n+1). Assume X_i is a nonempty standard Borel space and the complementary product Ω_{-i} = ∏_{j∈Fin(n)} X_{i.succAbove(j)} has measurable singletons. Write r_i(x) = (x_{i.succAbove(j)})_j and e_i(x) = (r_i(x), x_i). Let κ be the selected regular conditional-distribution kernel of the second coordinate given the first under (e_i)_#μ, and define H_i(x) = (e_i^{-1})_#(δ_{r_i(x)} × κ(r_i(x))). Then, for every x ∈ Ω whose complementary-coordinate fiber F_x = {y ∈ Ω : r_i(y) = r_i(x)} has nonzero μ-measure, H_i(x) = (μ(F_x))^{-1} • (μ restricted to F_x). Thus the coordinate heat-bath measure at every such x equals μ conditioned on that fiber.

source_review.evidence:
This review used only the designated anti-anchored packet. I did not inspect repository instructions, implementation bodies, prior reviews, repair suggestions, other agents' work, or external sources. Independence here means that the reviewer is distinct from the stated formalizer and blind decoder and assessed the supplied source evidence against their supplied artifacts independently.

The decisive finding is a direct mathematical counterexample on the finite Boolean domain itself. Let V = {0,1}, select v = 0, take x = (0,1), and let μ assign mass 1/4 to every configuration. Conditioning on the old complementary coordinate gives F_x = {(0,1),(1,1)} of mass 1/2. The reconstructed law is uniform on this fiber. The literal source instructions instead set the next second coordinate to x_0 = 0 and sample the first coordinate uniformly, yielding a law on {(0,0),(1,0)}. Thus the two laws differ even when every reconstructed assumption is satisfied. The selected-coordinate conditional marginal is compatible in this example; the nonselected-coordinate assignment is not.

The instruction pair suggests a possible indexing error in the pinned step 2, because step 3 conditions on old complementary values whereas step 2 overwrites those values with the old selected value. Nevertheless, the available evidence does not establish whether the published PDF contains that error, whether the packet excerpt is inaccurate, or whether omitted context changes its interpretation. Consequently, possible-source-error is a diagnosis of the supplied source representation, not a verified erratum to the publication.

Independently, positive complementary-fiber mass is a genuine qualification. It would follow from μ({x}) > 0 in the finite model, but the packet does not state that Ω is precisely positive-probability support or that the current state has positive mass. lean.statement:
∀ {n : ℕ} (μ : Measure (Fin (n + 1) → Bool)) [inst : IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
  (x y : Fin (n + 1) → Bool),
  μ {x} ≠ 0 →
    ((randomScan μ) x) {y} =
      (↑n + 1)⁻¹ *
        ∑ i,
          if ∀ (j : Fin (n + 1)), j ≠ i → y j = x j then
            (μ {z | (fun j => z (i.succAbove j)) = fun j => x (i.succAbove j)})⁻¹ * μ {y}
          else 0
decoder_context: Bool={false,true} has its standard discrete measurable structure; function spaces carry the product measurable structure. Measure and IsProbabilityMeasure denote a measure and total mass one. μ{x} is singleton mass in extended nonnegative reals.

For i:Fin(n+1), i.succAbove:Fin n→Fin(n+1) is the increasing bijection onto all indices except i. Define r_i(z)=(fun j=>z(i.succAbove j)) and e_i(z)=(r_i(z),z i); e_i is the corresponding measurable equivalence.

Write ν_i=(e_i)_#μ. Let C_i be the regular conditional distribution of the second component given the first under ν_i, selected as a Markov kernel by the ambient library. Set H_i(x)=(e_i⁻¹)_#(δ_{r_i(x)}⊗C_i(r_i(x))). Here # denotes pushforward and δ a Dirac measure.

randomScan μ is the finite sum over i:Fin(n+1) of H_i.withDensity(fun _ _ => (↑((n+1:ℝ≥0)⁻¹):ℝ≥0∞)); withDensity multiplies the component kernel's output measure by the stated constant density. The weights are state-independent.

source.original_text: Let E be a complete real inner-product space, s a convex subset, f:E→ℝ, g:E→E and m∈ℝ. Suppose f has ambient gradient g(z) at every z∈s. If ⟨g(y)−g(x),y−x⟩≥m‖y−x‖² for every x,y∈s, then f is m-strongly convex on s, in the chord sense with quadratic correction m/2.

lean.statement:
∀
  {E : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace E] {s : Set E}
  {f : E → ℝ} {m : ℝ} {grad : E → E},
  Convex ℝ s →
    (∀ z ∈ s, HasGradientAt f (grad z) z) →
      (∀ x ∈ s, ∀ y ∈ s, m * ‖y - x‖ ^ 2 ≤ inner ℝ (grad y - grad x) (y - x)) → StrongConvexOn s m f
decoder_context: E is a real normed additive group with a real inner product inducing its norm. CompleteSpace means that every Cauchy filter converges.
Convex ℝ s means that s contains a • x + b • y whenever x,y∈s, a,b≥0 and a+b=1.
HasGradientAt f (g z) z means that f has an ambient Frechet derivative at z represented by v ↦ inner ℝ (g z) v. It does not mean only a derivative within s.

StrongConvexOn s m f means Convex ℝ s and, for all x,y∈s and all nonnegative real a,b with a+b=1, f(a • x+b • y) ≤ a*f(x)+b*f(y)−a*b*(m/2*norm(x−y)^2). The definition itself imposes no sign restriction on m.

/-!
# Strong convexity from quantitative gradient monotonicity

Statement provenance: Optlib `Lower_Strong_Convex`, commit
`5da27c5f95aa6a8a45b8c14b968ade4c13ff18c3`,
`Optlib/Convex/StronglyConvex.lean` (Apache-2.0; Chenyi Li and Ziyu Wang).
The proof reuses Mathlib's scalar derivative criterion on an affine segment
after subtracting its quadratic correction. This is a mean-value-theorem route;
Chewi, arXiv:2605.07006v1, Proposition 1.6 (1.5) implies (1.3), instead uses
integration under whole-space C¹ assumptions. No integral proof, Hessian
equivalence or complete textbook proposition is claimed here.

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Analysis.StrongConvexGradientConverse

open Set
open scoped RealInnerProductSpace

variable {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [CompleteSpace E]

/-- Quantitative monotonicity of genuine ambient gradients on a convex domain
implies strong convexity, with the same (possibly signed) modulus. -/
theorem strongConvexOn_of_gradient_inner_lower_bound
    {s : Set E} {f : E → ℝ} {m : ℝ} {grad : E → E}
    (hs : Convex ℝ s)
    (hgrad : ∀ z ∈ s, HasGradientAt f (grad z) z)
    (hmono : ∀ x ∈ s, ∀ y ∈ s,
      m * ‖y - x‖ ^ 2 ≤ inner ℝ (grad y - grad x) (y - x)) :
    StrongConvexOn s m f := by
  refine ⟨hs, ?_⟩
  intro x hx y hy a b ha hb hab
  let p : ℝ → E := fun t => x + t • (y - x)
  let q : ℝ → ℝ := fun t => f (p t) - m / 2 * t ^ 2 * ‖y - x‖ ^ 2
  let q' : ℝ → ℝ := fun t => inner ℝ (grad (p t)) (y - x) - m * t * ‖y - x‖ ^ 2
  have hp : ∀ t ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, p t ∈ s := by
    intro t ht
    exact hs.add_smul_sub_mem hx hy ht
  have hq : ∀ t ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, HasDerivAt q (q' t) t := by
    intro t ht
    have hline : HasDerivAt (fun u => f (p u))
        (inner ℝ (grad (p t)) (y - x)) t := by
      have hpderiv : HasDerivAt p (y - x) t := by
        simpa [p] using ((hasDerivAt_id t).smul_const (y - x)).const_add x
      convert! (hgrad (p t) (hp t ht)).hasFDerivAt.comp_hasDerivAt t hpderiv using 1
    have hquad := (((hasDerivAt_id t).pow 2).const_mul (m / 2)).mul_const (‖y - x‖ ^ 2)
    convert! hline.sub hquad using 1
    simp only [q', id_eq]
    ring
  have hmon : MonotoneOn q' (Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) := by
    intro u hu v hv huv
    rcases eq_or_lt_of_le huv with rfl | huv
    · exact le_rfl
    have h := hmono (p u) (hp u hu) (p v) (hp v hv)
    have hdis : p v - p u = (v - u) • (y - x) := by
      simp only [p, add_sub_add_left_eq_sub, sub_smul]
    rw [hdis, inner_smul_right, norm_smul, Real.norm_eq_abs, mul_pow, sq_abs] at h
    have hscaled : (v - u) * (m * (v - u) * ‖y - x‖ ^ 2) ≤
        (v - u) * inner ℝ (grad (p v) - grad (p u)) (y - x) := by
      nlinarith [h]
    have hbound := le_of_mul_le_mul_left hscaled (sub_pos.mpr huv)
    rw [inner_sub_left] at hbound
    dsimp [q']
    linarith
  have hconv : ConvexOn ℝ (Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) q := by
    apply MonotoneOn.convexOn_of_deriv (convex_Icc (0 : ℝ) 1)
      (fun t ht => (hq t ht).continuousAt.continuousWithinAt)
      (fun t ht => (hq t (interior_subset ht)).differentiableAt.differentiableWithinAt)
    intro u hu v hv huv
    rw [(hq u (interior_subset hu)).deriv, (hq v (interior_subset hv)).deriv]
    exact hmon (interior_subset hu) (interior_subset hv) huv
  have hchord := hconv.2 (show (0 : ℝ) ∈ Icc 0 1 by norm_num)
    (show (1 : ℝ) ∈ Icc 0 1 by norm_num) ha hb hab
  have hpoint : a • x + b • y = p b := by
    have ha' : a = 1 - b := by linarith
    simp [p, ha', sub_smul, smul_sub]
    abel
  rw [hpoint]
  simp only [smul_eq_mul, mul_zero, mul_one, zero_add] at hchord ⊢
  norm_num [q, p] at hchord
  rw [norm_sub_rev] at hchord
  have ha' : a = 1 - b := by linarith
  rw [ha'] at hchord ⊢
  dsimp [p]
  nlinarith [hchord]

end AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Analysis.StrongConvexGradientConverse

steps.title: Stay on one segment
steps.text: Fix x,y in the domain, put d=y−x and N=‖d‖². Convexity of the domain keeps the full segment inside s. Subtract a scalar quadratic along that segment.
steps.lean: Local p and q select this segment; hp uses Convex.add_smul_sub_mem.

steps.title: Compute the genuine derivative
steps.text: Apply the chain rule to f composed with the affine segment, then differentiate the quadratic. The ambient gradient hypothesis supplies differentiability even at the endpoints. Therefore q is continuous on [0,1] and differentiable on its interior.
steps.lean: hq combines HasGradientAt.hasFDerivAt, HasFDerivAt.comp_hasDerivAt and derivatives of powers and scalar products.

steps.title: Cancel only a positive scalar
steps.text: For 0≤u<v≤1, the displacement is p(v)−p(u)=(v−u)d. Apply the gradient bound and divide by the positive parameter difference. Subtracting the quadratic derivative gives monotonicity of q′. Equal parameters require no division.
steps.lean: hdis rewrites the displacement. hscaled rewrites norm_smul using |v−u|²=(v−u)². le_of_mul_le_mul_left cancels v−u>0; hmon handles equality separately.

steps.title: Use scalar convexity
steps.text: The mean value theorem implies that a continuous scalar function with nondecreasing derivative is convex on the interval. All three hypotheses have been established, so the chord bound for q follows.
steps.lean: hconv applies Mathlib MonotoneOn.convexOn_of_deriv. hq.deriv identifies the library derivative with the supplied q′. hchord evaluates the resulting ConvexOn inequality at 0 and 1.

steps.title: Restore the quadratic correction
steps.text: Expand q at the three parameters and use a=1−b. The difference between b and b² is ab, producing exactly the strong-convexity correction. Nothing here requires m≥0.
steps.lean: hpoint identifies ax+by with p(b). norm_sub_rev aligns norm conventions; substitution of a=1−b and ring arithmetic finish the inequality.

reconstruction.text: Let E be a complete real inner product space, let s be any convex subset of E, let f : E → ℝ and grad : E → E, and let m ∈ ℝ. Suppose that f is Fréchet differentiable in the ambient space at every z ∈ s, with derivative v ↦ ⟨grad(z), v⟩. Suppose further that for every x,y ∈ s, m‖y−x‖² ≤ ⟨grad(y)−grad(x), y−x⟩. Then f is strongly convex on s with parameter m in the following precise sense: for every x,y ∈ s and every a,b ∈ ℝ with a ≥ 0, b ≥ 0 and a+b=1, f(ax+by) ≤ af(x)+bf(y)−(m/2)ab‖x−y‖². Convexity of s is also part of the conclusion. No sign restriction is imposed on m.
